title: The marathon that took 54 years to finish
description:
Shizo Kanakuri, one of Japan's first two Olympians, collapsed from heat 16 miles into the 1912 Stockholm Olympic marathon, recovered at a stranger's garden party, and - too ashamed to report his withdrawal - quietly went home to Japan. Sweden listed him as a missing person for 50 years.
In 1967, Swedish television found him, 75 years old, and invited him back to finish his race. Official time: 54 years, 8 months, 6 days, 5 hours, 32 minutes, 20.3 seconds - the slowest marathon ever completed, and a record that can never be broken. He went on to found Japan's Hakone Ekiden and is celebrated as the father of Japanese marathon running.
